body.p: As stated above, Applicant appreciates the Examiner's thorough examination of the subject application and requests reexamination and reconsideration of the subject application in view of the preceding amendments and the following remarks.

As of the subject action, claims 1-30 were pending in the subject application, of which claims 1, 19, and 27 are independent claims. With this Response, Applicant has amended claims 1, 4-6, 14-16, 19, 21-23, and 27-30 and has cancelled claims 17-18. Applicant respectfully submits that no new matter is believed to have been entered as a result of this Response. All objections and rejections are respectfully traversed.

Claims 4-6, 14-17, 21-23, and 28-30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections. Without conceding the rejection, Applicant has amended claims 4-6, 14-16, 21-23, and 28-30. For example, claim 4 has been amended to recite features of the pneumatic control subsystem, claim 5 has been amended to recite features of the electric control subsystem, and claim 6 has been amended to recite features of the hydraulic control subsystem. Claims 14-16 have been amended to recite the features of the robotic arm subsystem. Claim 17 has been cancelled. As such, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 4-6, 14-17, 21-23, and 28-30 meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).

Claims 1-3, 5, 12-20, 22, 27, and 29 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Edinger et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,346,160, hereinafter referred to as "Edinger"). Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Without conceding the rejection and in an effort to accelerate prosecution of the subject application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 19, and 27. Representative independent claim 1 is recited below for convenience:

Support for these amendments may be found in at least dependent claim 18 and paragraph [0019] of the subject application as published, which are reproduced below for convenience.

Applicant respectfully submits that Edinger fails to teach, disclose, or even suggest "a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous mobile base". For example, in rejecting dependent claim 18, the subject action states "Edinger illustrates the moveable operating platform is a non- autonomous mobile base". See, subject action, p. 5. FIGS. 1 and 3 of Edinger are reproduced below for convenience.

As can be seen from at least FIGS. 1 and 3, Edinger is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, where the operating platform is an autonomous mobile base. As such, Applicants respectfully submit that Edinger is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest Applicant's claimed "a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous mobile base."
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-3, 5, 12-20, 22, 27, and 29 under § 102 as being anticipated by Edinger be withdrawn.

Claims 4, 6-11, 21, 23-26, 28, and 30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Edinger as applied to claims 1, 19, and 27 above, and further in view of Gilbertson et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,827,678, hereinafter referred to as "Gilbertson"). Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

As noted above, Edinger fails to teach, disclose, or suggest "a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous mobile base". The addition of Gilbertson fails to remedy the deficiencies of Edinger. Accordingly, the combination of Edinger and Gilbertson fails to render claims 4, 6-11, 21, 23-26, 28, and 30 unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
Reply to Office Action of: June 16, 2022 Attorney Docket No.: 108622.00013

In this response, Applicant has amended various claims and/or asserted arguments in this application to facilitate expeditious prosecution of the application. Applicant is not conceding that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to the instant action, and/or having interpretations other than presented herein are unpatentable over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by any claims prior to this response, claims having different interpretations than presented in this response, and additional claims.

In consideration of the amendments and foregoing discussion, Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is in condition for allowance. While Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is now in condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to telephone Applicant's representative (617-854-1420) to facilitate prosecution of this application. Please apply any charges or credits to the above-noted deposit account.
